what-the-gospel-actually-is.metaDescription: The gospel is not advice on how to be good or feel loved. It is news about something God has done, and news asks more of you than advice.

what-is-the-kingdom-of-god-and-why-it-ch.metaDescription: The kingdom of God is not heaven when you die, and not a project you build. Once you see what Jesus meant by it, the rest of the Bible reads differently.

what-christian-nationalism-is-and-is-not.metaDescription: Christian nationalism gets thrown as an insult in both directions. A pastor on what the phrase actually names, and what it does not.

how-to-read-the-bible-without-making-it-.metaDescription: Two honest readers open the same page and find opposite gods. The Bible is not unclear. Nobody reads from nowhere. How to read it without bending it.

already-and-not-yet-living-between-two-w.metaDescription: Faith that feels like victory and defeat at once is not failure. The New Testament says you live in the overlap of two ages. Here is what that changes.

why-there-are-so-many-christian-denomina.metaDescription: The thirty thousand denominations number is a misused statistic. The stubborn fact is how much divided Christians still confess in common.

the-atheist-in-the-pulpit.metaDescription: A pastor who was an atheist with real reasons tells the honest story of what changed his mind, slowly and against his own preference, and what it cost him.

christendom-is-ending.metaDescription: For seventeen centuries, being born in the West meant being born Christian. That arrangement is dying, and most of the church is grieving the wrong thing.

when-the-church-is-what-hurt-you.metaDescription: Church hurt is real, and naming it is not bitterness. A pastor on the wound the institution causes, and the God who is furious about it.

does-god-actually-exist.metaDescription: A pastor who spent years as an atheist on why he stopped: not because someone won an argument, but because his own view could not pay its bills.

is-jesus-really-the-only-way.metaDescription: A former atheist on the claim he once found obscene: that Jesus is the only way. The objection at full strength, and the one question it cannot survive.

suffering-without-explanation.metaDescription: Everyone shows up with a reason for suffering. Job spends thirty seven chapters refusing every one, and when God finally speaks he gives none either.

can-you-have-faith-and-doubt.metaDescription: You were told real Christians do not have questions. The Hebrew word for faith says the opposite: not certainty, but a steadiness that can carry weight.

why-does-god-feel-far-away.metaDescription: Feeling that God is far away is not a conclusion you reasoned your way to. It is the weather of our age. A pastor who came from atheism on why.

did-the-resurrection-happen.metaDescription: Everything in Christianity hangs on one event that either happened or did not. The historical case for the resurrection, made the way a skeptic deserves.

can-you-trust-the-bible.metaDescription: The Bible is not what most people think it is, on either side of the argument. It is stranger, more honest, and tougher than the stories told about it.

what-if-we-are-wrong.metaDescription: The question shows up at night: what if the whole thing is a story we told ourselves? A faith that cannot survive that question was never faith.

what-psalms-teach-about-anger-at-god.metaDescription: The church taught you that anger at God is a sin. The prayer book God gave us is full of it, and his own Son died with a complaint on his lips.

how-do-you-actually-pray.metaDescription: Most people want to pray and have no idea how to begin. The answer is not a formula. It is closer to learning to talk with someone already in the room.

done-with-church-not-jesus.metaDescription: Millions have walked out of church without walking away from Jesus. That is not a contradiction to fix. It is a wound to name, and a question to ask.

why-did-jesus-have-to-die.metaDescription: The cross is the most recognized symbol on earth and the least understood. Why a death, and why that death? The church has more than one answer.

anxiety-and-faith.metaDescription: The verse arrives at three in the morning and does not comfort. Under the racing heart is a worse fear: that the anxiety itself is the sin.
